criteria.reason: Both copies of §3.6a say 'Nothing is asked and nothing stops (D1)': a needs-owner environment is a flag and the build carries on. The AskUserQuestion grep shows no use tied to an environment.
verify-build step 2 says 'Nothing is asked in any mode (D1)'. An environment that needs the owner takes the default, and ISSUES names it.

The persisted state shape documents status needs-owner with reason, need and default 'criteria needing it resolve not_verifiable'. §8.1a (implement-trd.md around line 1697) resolves those criteria not_verifiable.
The readout ISSUES template adds one line per needs-owner environment: '{environment} needs you: {need}', with 'You act' as the owner's action.

The grep of the changed command files shows no environment-tied AskUserQuestion. A judge-side grep of the changed lib and workflow files found no AskUserQuestion at all. The only STUCK added in the diff is the 'COMMAND COMPLETE (not STUCK)' wording. §3.6a records status plus default for each check.

Jest passed 562/562. One test asserts the call order setup, exercise, judge, with Setup before Exercise. The 'checks only targets that hold an open criterion' test shows two setup calls across two iterations. decideSetup's per-environment result carries reachable, build and holder.
With no identity method declared, decideSetup returns build 'unknown', action proceed, no problems, and a flag. The matching Jest test passes.

The Debug stage reported this as unbuilt: the setup check decides 'held by another checkout' only from processes listening on declared ports. Nothing detects a process holding a declared non-port resource, because the setup targets carry ports and no resource field. The port half works (iteration 1: a listener outside the checkout was reported held, naming its directory; one inside was not).

Jest passes: 'dispatches exactly one setup-refresh on a refresh return', 'a setup-refresh that still fails ends setup-failure', and 'ends setup-failure on a setup-refresh that asks for a second refresh'. The loop refreshes once and never a second time.
Jest 'dispatches one Record agent and no Judge, Debug or Render' passes for the setup-failure exit.
With a setup-failure history, decide-next returns exit-setup-failure at iterations 2 to 5 where the same ordinary input returns exit-stalled.

On the final permitted iteration (5 of 5), decide-next returns exit-setup-failure; the ordinary case returns exit-stuck. On the workflow side, Jest shows a setup failure ending the run with no Judge or Debug.
The rendered report has one Setup line per problem, each naming the problem and its fix: build not HEAD, and port held by another checkout at a named path.

The outcome line reads 'Setup Failure', a label distinct from Stalled and Stuck. The report's Reason line says 'the environment, not the code' and its Next line says 'fix the environment named above'.
Both identical copies of implement-trd.md: the banner is COMMAND COMPLETE, not STUCK, and names setup-failure and the first problem. §3.6a never stops the run.
verify-build step 5 renders setup-failure as 'not checked because the environment is broken, not the code', and its NEXT carve-out tells the owner to fix the environment.

refine-verification leads with 'the environment, not the code' and turns no open criterion into a Blocker or fix task. fix-plan.js answers setup-failure by committing with a flag, and its Jest test passes.
The plan.md light template has the '## Verification Environment' heading with its three lines: Environment, Refresh, Cannot be checked there.
trd-authoring.md Section 9b has the same three lines, and its mirror copy is byte-identical.
§3.6a treats absence as valid: target source none, a DECISIONS line, no error. No code parser reads the section (checked in lib, workflows and hooks), so the text reading step is the whole check.
§3.6a takes the section's named environment as the run's target with source trd, and §8.1a reads the section for setupTargets.
